thread:
Samira (CS): FYI — AcmeCorp just hit 82% of their monthly credits in the last 36h. Renewal call in 9 days. Need an action plan to avoid sticker shock and show we're on it.
Ben (AE): Ugh. Is that mainly embeddings or generation?
Samira (CS): Mostly generation. They spiked a few long-running batch jobs last week after the new importer landed.
Jules (Solutions Eng): I can audit their routes and suggest a quick throttling + batching tweak. Can we get access to their request patterns?
Samira (CS): Yes, they granted read-only view this morning. I pulled the top 10 routes. Sharing highlights: high concurrency on /v1/generate, lots of repeated prefixes.
OpsBot: alert: account_usage.acmecorp > 75% of monthly_credits (triggered at 2829156791).
Kira (Finance): Also flagging: if they exceed 90% before renewal, finance will need to re-run the renewal tier math.
Ben (AE): Prioritize fixes that don't block product. Customer is sensitive to experience — no hard cutoff unless we coordinate.
Jules (Solutions Eng): Proposed short steps: 1) Apply soft throttle at 70% of baseline per route. 2) Enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. 3) Suggest lightweight quantized model for bulk exports.
Jules (Solutions Eng): Snippet for Ops to apply a soft throttle rule in Console:
```yaml
rule_name: acmecorp-soft-throttle
scope: organization:acmecorp
condition: request_rate > baseline * 1.2
action: reduce_concurrency_to: 0.7
notify: [samira@redwood.com, ben@redwood.com]
```
Samira (CS): Love it — that preserves UX and reduces burn. Can we also prepare a 1-pager for the renewal call showing the steps and impact?
Ben (AE): I'll own the 1-pager with a simple before/after cost table and recommended commit level.
Kira (Finance): I can run the numbers for commit scenarios. What baseline should I use for the 'after' projection?
Jules (Solutions Eng): Use projected 30% reduction for generator-heavy jobs if caching + throttle applied, 10-15% if they adopt quantized model for exports.
Samira (CS): I'll schedule an enablement runbook with Acme's SREs for tomorrow 10am PT and capture feedback on the importer behavior.
Ben (AE): @Samira please add the one-pager to the shared drive and tag me. I'll ask exec sponsor to join renewal call.
OpsBot: deploy: rule acmecorp-soft-throttle queued by Jules at 2829156842.
Jules (Solutions Eng): Deployed soft throttle to staging, rolling to prod after 10m testing. Logs look good.
Samira (CS): After 20m in prod: tail shows 18% reduction in tokens generation and no 5xxs. Good sign.
Kira (Finance): Based on current trajectory, with soft throttle we'll likely land at ~76% month burn — that keeps them in current tier and limits pricing negotiation leverage.
Ben (AE): Action items: Ben — prep 1-pager; Samira — runbook + SRE notes; Jules — follow-up audit for caching opportunity; Kira — commit scenarios.
Samira (CS): Also tagging feedback capture: they asked for per-route cost labels in Console UI. I'll log as product feedback (low-to-mid priority).
Ben (AE): Noted. For renewal call let's lead with data: 24h spike root cause, corrective actions taken, projected spend curve. Keep it tight.
Samira (CS): I'll post a short thread summary and attach the graphs before EOD. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Jules (Solutions Eng): One more thought — we should include a temporary usage cap proposal the customer can opt into for the last week of the cycle. Soft cap + alert to their SRE avoids surprises.
Kira (Finance): If they opt in we can offer a small one-time credit to smooth renewal negotiations. I'll compute impact.
Samira (CS): Great. I'll include the opt-in cap option in the 1-pager.
Ben (AE): Perfect. Meeting scheduled for next Wed 9am PT. Everyone please review artifacts beforehand.
Samira (CS): Summary pinned to this thread when ready.
OpsBot: note: ticket CS-8247 created for Acme runbook and follow-ups.
